evidence.note: After reading the contract, the agent lays out design decisions and a module build order (parser → evaluator → functions → workbook → store → server → xlsx) that follows the real dependency chain — more than a flat to-do list, but stated as prose rather than an explicit milestone hierarchy with done-criteria.

The agent built the entire ~150-function engine breadth before ever standing up the server/health/persistence loop, contrary to anchor-8's 'get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core round-trip green before breadth' — breadth was front-loaded ahead of the load-bearing skeleton.
Uses the runnable dev suite as a concrete done-check at a checkpoint ('123/131 passing'), tying progress to verifiable test results — a rough-checkpoint pattern between anchors 5 and 8.

Once all 131 smoke tests are green, deliberately re-orients into a distinct hidden-suite hardening phase (performance, persistence, xlsx round-trip, edge cases), showing some staged re-sequencing rather than a single undifferentiated push.

Hardening phase proceeds as a sensible sequence of targeted probes with implicit pass/fail checks, but the ordering is reactive and the per-item plans stay tactical rather than a living, risk-ranked milestone plan (short of anchor 10).

reasoning: The agent clearly phases the work into dependency-ordered stages (contract → engine core → server/persistence → smoke-suite green → hidden-suite hardening) and repeatedly uses the runnable dev suite as done-checks at checkpoints, which is above the flat, unordered anchor-5 list. However, it never articulated an explicit milestone hierarchy with pre-declared done-criteria, and it front-loaded the full ~150-function breadth before proving a live-server/persistence/core round-trip skeleton green — the specific pattern anchor 8 requires. That places it between 5 and 8, at a 6.
